lessons.title: What Stands in the Way Becomes the Way
lessons.key_idea: Obstacles are not detours from your path but raw material you can use to move forward.

lessons.title: See the Problem Clearly and Calmly
lessons.key_idea: The first discipline is perception: steady your nerves and judge events objectively, without adding fear or drama.

lessons.title: Focus Only on What You Control
lessons.key_idea: Separate what is up to you from what is not, and put all your energy into the part you can actually change.

lessons.title: Act With Persistence and Iteration
lessons.key_idea: The second discipline is action: keep trying, testing and adjusting, one small step at a time, until the problem gives way.

lessons.title: Go Around, or Use It Against Itself
lessons.key_idea: When a direct attack fails, try an indirect approach or turn the obstacle's own force into your advantage.

lessons.title: Anticipate Trouble, Then Embrace What Happens
lessons.key_idea: The third discipline is will: imagine what could go wrong in advance, and learn to accept, even love, whatever actually happens.

lessons.title: Persevere and Be Ready to Begin Again
lessons.key_idea: Perception, action and will work together, so that every obstacle you overcome simply prepares you for the next one.

plan.title: The Obstacle Is the Way
plan.author: Ryan Holiday
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's structure, its three-part framework of perception, action and will, and many of its main historical examples well, though I may not recall every minor detail.
plan.one_liner: Ancient Stoic wisdom for turning every setback, frustration and roadblock into fuel for moving forward.
plan.summary: Ryan Holiday takes a line from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius and builds a practical philosophy around it. The obstacle in front of you is not just something to get past. It can become the path itself. Drawing on Stoic thinkers like Epictetus and Seneca, Holiday organizes the book around three disciplines. Perception means seeing problems clearly and calmly, without panic or self-pity. Action means attacking problems with persistence, creativity and steady effort. Will means building an inner resilience that accepts what cannot be changed and keeps going anyway. Along the way he tells stories of people who turned hardship into advantage, including Rockefeller staying cool in a financial panic, Grant at Vicksburg, and Edison after a devastating fire. The result is a short, energizing guide to handling adversity.
